what_its_for: Ozanimod is used to treat adults with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS) — including relapsing-remitting MS — to help reduce the number of MS flare-ups (relapses) and slow disability progression. It is also used to treat adults with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis (UC), a type of inflammatory bowel disease that causes swelling and sores in the large intestine.
how_to_take: Take ozanimod by mouth, exactly as your doctor prescribes. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush, chew, or open it. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Because this medicine affects your heart rate when you first start it, your doctor will have you start on a lower dose for the first week or two before moving to the full dose — this is called a 'starter pack.' Follow the starter pack schedule carefully.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 0.23 mg once daily for the first 4 days, then 0.46 mg once daily for days 5 through 7, and then the full maintenance dose of 0.92 mg once daily from day 8 onward. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be adjusted based on your condition and how you respond to the medicine.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Do not double up to make up for a missed dose. Important: If you miss doses during the first 2 weeks of treatment (the starter period), call your doctor before restarting — you may need to begin the starter pack schedule again from the beginning, which requires heart monitoring.
storage: Store ozanimod at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the capsules in their original container with the cap tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking certain medications that interact with ozanimod, including some antidepressants (MAOIs such as phenelzine or selegiline) — this combination can cause a dangerous reaction. Avoid live vaccines while taking ozanimod and for up to 3 months after stopping, as this medicine weakens your immune system. Avoid contact with people who are sick or have infections. Limit foods that are very high in tyramine (such as aged cheeses, cured meats, and red wine), as ozanimod may interact with tyramine and raise your blood pressure. Avoid becoming pregnant — use effective birth control while taking ozanimod and for 3 months after your last dose. Do not stop taking ozanimod without talking to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: slow or irregular heartbeat, chest pain, or shortness of breath (especially when you first start the medicine); signs of infection such as fever, chills, body aches, or unusual fatigue; vision changes, eye pain, or blurred vision (could be a sign of a serious eye problem called macular edema); signs of a serious brain infection called PML — confusion, memory problems, weakness on one side of the body, or trouble speaking; sudden severe headache, stiff neck, or sensitivity to light (signs of meningitis); signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain; unusual swelling or lumps; or if you are planning to become pregnant or think you may be pregnant.
when_it_works: Ozanimod starts working in your body right away, but you may not notice improvements in your symptoms for several weeks to months. For MS, your doctor will monitor you with MRI scans and check for relapses over time. For ulcerative colitis, some patients see improvement in symptoms within 10 weeks, but it may take longer. Keep taking your medicine even if you feel well — stopping without your doctor's guidance can cause your condition to return or worsen.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do not use ozanimod during pregnancy — it may harm the unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 3 months after stopping. Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Children: Ozanimod is not approved for use in patients under 18 years old. Older adults: Older patients may have a higher risk of certain side effects, including infections and heart-related effects — your doctor will monitor you closely. Heart conditions: If you have certain heart problems (such as recent heart attack, heart failure, or certain heart rhythm issues), this medicine may not be safe for you — talk to your doctor about your heart history before starting. Liver disease: Ozanimod is not recommended for patients with severe liver problems. Vaccinations: Make sure all your vaccines are up to date before starting ozanimod. Talk to your doctor at least 1 month before starting if you need any live vaccines.
